newsitem.title: CANADA: CANADIAN FRACMASTER CEO TO FOCUS ON OTHER BUSINESS.
newsitem.headline: CANADIAN FRACMASTER CEO TO FOCUS ON OTHER BUSINESS.

text.p: Canadian Fracmaster Ltd Chairman Alfred Balm will focus on his other business interests after selling a controlling C$550 million stake in the oil services company, he said Wednesday.
In a statement issued from his home base of Geneva, Switzerland, Balm said he was retiring from Fracmaster at a time when the company's outlook was rosy.
"The company is virtually debt free and is strategically well positioned at home and abroad," the Dutch-born businessman said.

Calgary-based Fracmaster, an international oil services company that operates primarily in the North American and Russian energy sectors, said late Tuesday that Balm would sell his 67.5 million interest and step down as chief executive.
After the secondary offering is completed in September, President Les Margetak would become chief executive, the company said.
Balm, who took Fracmaster public in 1993, owns 28.9 million shares, which at their current price are worth almost C$550 million.

Balm said he would devote his energy to his other investments, which include information management firm QC Data, which "is presently targeting strategic acquisitions worldwide." ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
